title: Head-tracked 3D portal
blurb: A recessed 3D portal room in WebGL 2 with three depth-layered HTML cards driven by an asymmetric off-axis frustum from pointer drag, device tilt or FaceDetector, plus an AR mode that pins a live HTML card onto a BarcodeDetector QR quad.
question: Can FaceDetector or BarcodeDetector drive an asymmetric off-axis 3D frustum or pin live interactive HTML onto a detected barcode over a live camera feed, and does updateElementGeometry() keep hit-testing aligned under 60 fps off-axis perspective matrices?
result: Not verified yet in a live browser. One ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas draws a recessed grid room with three depth-layered HTML cards (z = +0.15, -0.35 and -0.85) under an off-axis frustum, updates each card's hit box via updateElementGeometry() and geometryUnit(), and switches on tap to FaceDetector head tracking or BarcodeDetector 4-corner homography over a camera feed or synthetic QR marker.
